description: Per-container control-plane usage of each kube-burner run, written by combine_usage.py

fields.trust: how much to trust the run, from the hand-written notes file: good, caveats or low
fields.notes: why, from the hand-written notes file
fields.memory_gib: memory working set in GiB; percentiles are of the readings as recorded
fields.cpu_cores: CPU in cores; percentiles are of 5-minute averages, so p50 is close to the sustained average use
fields.total: the whole control plane's actual total over the window: p50 and p95 of the sum of every container's readings at each moment (for CPU, of 5-minute averages of that sum). Use this for the cluster's p95, rather than adding up containers' p95s. filled_in is the share of the summed readings that were missing and filled in along a straight line from the copy's neighboring readings
fields.copies: how many copies (pods) count: those with readings for at least half the window, which leaves out copies being replaced; it can differ between memory and CPU
fields.busiest_copy: the highest p50 and the highest p95 among the copies, each taken separately, so they can come from different copies; every copy reserves the same, so this is what a reservation has to fit
fields.average_copy: the p50 and p95 averaged over the copies; copies x p50, added up over all containers, closely matches the cluster's typical total use. p95s don't add up like that: containers don't peak at the same moment, so the sum overstates the cluster's p95
fields.readings_present: share of the expected readings that exist, over the copies that count (for a run, over all its containers); below 1 means missing data or, for CPU, an idle container, as the CPU metric drops readings of exactly zero
fields.raw_peak: highest single CPU reading of any copy, before averaging

notes_for_all_runs: Each size has only one test run, so how much its numbers would vary between runs is unknown. The runs also weren't set up the same way: three OpenShift versions (4.19, 4.20, 4.22), four kube-burner versions (1.6.9, 1.7.9, 1.8.0, 1.11.12), a 30-second or 2-minute churn delay, and churn phases that actually lasted 20 to 63 minutes (most were set to 20), so comparing sizes partly compares setups. The shortest churn phases (20 to 23 minutes: 3, 6 and 12 nodes at 100 QPS, 30 and 49 nodes) give few 5-minute averages, so their CPU p95 is close to the highest value.

runs.notes: Memory is complete, but only 74% of CPU readings exist, so its CPU numbers, especially peaks, are less reliable. Its CPU graph marks the moments that read low, and its totals fill in the missing readings. Runs a newer OpenShift (4.20) than most runs (4.19).

Only 72% of CPU readings exist and a few memory readings are missing, so its CPU numbers, especially peaks, are less reliable. Its graphs mark the moments that read low, and its totals fill in the missing readings. Runs a newer OpenShift (4.20) than most runs (4.19).

Complete data. Set to 100 QPS, but kube-burner only reached about 6 queries per second, against about 4.7 in the 20 QPS run, so its load was only a little higher. Uses about 2 GiB more memory than the other 12-node run, mostly kube-apiserver.

Complete data. Its churn phase was set to 30 minutes instead of the usual 20, and an earlier kube-apiserver rollout was just finishing as churn began (the last old copy's last reading is 12 seconds into it), which barely affects the numbers.

Complete data, but a different setup from the other runs: newer OpenShift (4.22, most runs are 4.19) and kube-burner (1.11.12) versions, and the only run with a router. Uses more memory than the 60-node run.
Complete data, with a long churn phase (36 minutes).

Complete once its duplicate records are removed, which the scripts do, with a long churn phase (63 minutes).

No churn phase, and memory climbs until near the end: memory comes from its last 10 minutes, once it has leveled off, and CPU from the whole run, which is all create phase and so a conservative (high) estimate. The memory may be a few percent low, as in the large runs (60 to 250 nodes) churn-phase memory was 0 to 8% above the end of their create phase. Ran with 498 workers. Its duplicate records are removed by the scripts.
